utterances.text: See, at the time, they also took me in for an interview prior to that, and then released me. So up until the 5th of June -- do you want me to give you the names of the people who were imprisoned on the 25th of June?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You can give me a number, if you like, a number of people.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can also give you the names of the people from my village, Hadzic Hasan, Hadzic Enes with two brothers, Hadzic Selim, Hadzic Edhem, with brothers Hadzic Edin. The brothers Smail Hadzic, Ahmo, Jusuf, Nasuf and Vejiz Hadzic. From Kalinovik: Jasarevic Hilmo, Hatic Adil, Vranovic Salko, Musanovic Safet, Bajric Ibro, Redzovic Rasid, Salcic Muzaref --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Vihovici [phoen] village, the following were imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, I think Ms. Loukas indicated that she'd like to know approximately the number of people that were detained on the 25th of June. I do understand that you know them all, but you'll understand that having all their names is not of great importance for us, although of course this Chamber is well aware that these were all individuals you knew that were then arrested. So if you could indicate a number, not because these persons as such are not of any importance, but because here the number is rather important than the exact names of them.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th of June, about 71 of us were taken prisoner. One was released that same day. One escaped. One was released for health reasons. And on the 31st of July, they brought 11 new people in, amongst whom there was Dr. Abdurahman Filipovic, who worked in the health centre in Kalinovik as a doctor, which means that there were, on the 1st of August, 1992, in the camp, 85 inmates. At that time, in the primary school building, we came across another 14 people who had been taken into custody in Trnovo and there were some post office-workers there who were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also indicate in that paragraph that you were interrogated and released. At about what time period are we talking about there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime in May. I can't remember the exact date, but I do know that Visnjevac came to get me. I can't remember his first name. He was in the crime department and he took me from my office in my company for interrogation, and they said that I had had contacts with the Green Berets, which I never did have. And had I had those kinds of contacts, I wouldn't have left Kalinovik and survived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And still Ms. Loukas does not know how long approximately you were there for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About half an hour. That's how long I was interrogated for.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you refer in that paragraph to being shouted at and having stupid questions asked of you. What questions did they ask you? You've already indicated that they were questions in relation to your involvement with the Green Berets. Was anything else asked of you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he asked me why people were meeting in my house, why my neighbours came to my house, why my relatives -- one of my relatives came to sit around in the evening, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I'm just looking at the time. I'm anxious to ensure, working in conjunction with the witness, the Trial Chamber, and what have you, that I do finish this afternoon, and I think it's potentially possible, but I don't think it's possible in ten minutes, in view of the nature of the way that the questions are taking a little longer to be answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, I'm also looking at the technicians and the interpreters whether we could take a bit more time, but we have not reserved the courtroom for this afternoon. So we should then be within the limits, and with the cooperation of all those assisting us. So if you'd please keep that in mind, and I hardly dare to ask the interpreters, but I have not heard any no until now.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hadzic, let's go to paragraphs 23, 24, and 25 of your statement. And in particular, 25. You basically set out there, do you agree with me, your theory of what occurred? Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course, you would tell the Trial Chamber, that is, that is in essence your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you base that on what occurred to you in Kalinovik; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, obviously, you'd be prepared to concede that there are potentially other theories than the one you hold.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to -- in fact, moving back to paragraph 9. You've indicated there that it is your strong belief that these units were there to deliberately intimidate. Do you see that? Have you got that before you, Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We gained the impression that they were there to intimidate us, because they had no reason to be in Kalinovik, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, being absolutely fair, of course, Mr. Hadzic, you would concede that there are other possible interpretations than the units being there to deliberately intimidate; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, time did tell that the units were actually there to intimidate us, because they said that they had come there to protect the Serb people in Kalinovik, and several villages around Kalinovik, where there are about 500 Muslims. And from that it would emerge that they had really come to instil fear in us, because they said they came to defend the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Hadzic. But you would tell the Trial Chamber basically that your opinion is, based on what you saw, that that's what -- that's how you formed your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just going to your paragraph 4 in your statement. Do you have that before you, Mr. Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, again, that's an expression of opinion from you.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is based on what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course, you would have to fairly concede that you don't have any specific knowledge of events at a very high level; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I do know what happened to those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, in general terms, if the words in the statements are used like "I believe" without any further support in facts, then the Chamber of course would evaluate that as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not as a hidden -- not as a belief with a lot of hidden facts supporting it. It would be considered to be a personal impression based on the kind of things the witness tells us. So that's a starting point. It's not always necessary to verify that with the witness, because that will be the starting point for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, but I do like to underline these things for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. And also that basically -- well, in fact I'll move on to another topic, Your Honour. In view of Your Honour's intervention, I don't think I need to ask any further questions on that issue. And I'll in fact move on to some -- in relation to the question of the supplemental information. Now, of course, Mr. Hadzic, you gave your statement to the International Criminal Tribunal over five years ago now; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, of course, you knew that when the Prosecution came to speak to you, they were, of course, anxious to find the people responsible for what had occurred in Kalinovik?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And obviously, they told you to tell them everything that you knew; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course, they took down everything you said?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course, in relation to your ICTY statement, you indicated that you'd dealt with a lot of matters, of course, in your previous Bosnian statement, but that you were able to add certain information that you have additionally recalled since making it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, obviously, the people from the Prosecution, when they were interviewing you, were interested in knowing exactly what had occurred to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And they were obviously interested in the time -- at the time in obtaining from you whether you had any information about connections to a higher level; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you were, of course, careful to ensure that you told them everything you knew?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And it wasn't just a question of answering their specific questions; whenever you could, you gave them all additional information you had. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the information that I gave to the Bosnian authorities as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Hadzic. Now, Mr. Hadzic, you've supplied the Prosecution with additional information yesterday; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that additional information included that Grujo Lalovic also said at this meeting that he had received "orders from above" and referred to order from Trebinje; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So the situation is, of course, that you now supply this additional information in relation to orders from above, 12 years after the events in question; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I gave that information about those events to the Bosnian authorities already in 1992. And yesterday I saw that the Prosecution had that statement of mine, and that's when I mentioned Grujo Lalovic, Nikola Kovac, Bosko Govedarica, head of the SUP, et cetera. So I thought that those statements were a component part of the overall statement, and I substantiated that talking to the Prosecution yesterday about the people who were there at the time and held those posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There's no dispute, Mr. Hadzic, that there are two Bosnian statements that incorporate -- are incorporated within your material for the ICTY statement. My question is this: That you did not in those three documents refer to Grujo Lalovic saying that he had received orders from above and referring to orders from Trebinje. You'd agree with me on that proposition?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the meeting, when we handed over the weapons, that's when he told us that the order had come from Trebinje level, that they wouldn't take away our weapons but that they had received the order from Trebinje and had to do so. I think that that's what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I stop you. Ms. Loukas would like to know whether you agree that a statement to that extent, that is, that he told that during that meeting, does not appear in your previous statements. So that this is the first time you tell this. That's what she'd like to verify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All right. Probably I didn't say then, that then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hadzic, so you've conceded that you now say it for the first time, 12 years after the event, and of course that you didn't mention it in your statement five years ago either; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it would seem. But I gave -- if you take the other commission I gave a report to the authorities, to the investigations commission, I have an item saying that I blamed Grujo Lalovic for it all. All right. I didn't say that he had received the order from Trebinje. I didn't mention that. But, you know, it was all a situation of trauma, a traumatic situation when I was giving those statements. So I didn't actually mention that then, but I say so now.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. Hadzic, but of course you've had an opportunity to give a number of those statements and you've never mentioned it in any of those statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the statements. You can ask the witness five times whether he agrees that it's not in the statement, but it really makes no -- it really doesn't assist the Chamber. The point is entirely clear that you draw the attention of this Chamber to the fact that this new element that arose yesterday does not appear in his earlier statements. That's perfectly clear to us. So if there's any further question, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, one -- perhaps the process is most easily short circuited by a concession from the Prosecution that it does not appear in the earlier statements, the "order from above" aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As His Honour has pointed out, that is in fact the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Your Honour, in view of that, and I also notice the clock, the areas that I need to cover have been covered and I think that the witness, unless there are any further questions from the Bench, I think we're going to come within time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, is there any need to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No need at all. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, since the Chamber has no further questions to you, this concludes your testimony in this court. First of all, I'd like to thank you for coming from quite a distance to The Hague and to answer all the questions that have been put to you by the Prosecution, by the Defence, because the Chamber is well aware that from the content of your testimony in all respects, that is, what happened then and what you're still suffering, as you told us, at this very moment, that it certainly would not have been easy to do that. We highly appreciate that you came, and we wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to add to that that if there were a few moments where you could have told us far more, it's not due to any lack of interest that we didn't hear further details. But first of all, we have read your statement, and of course there are other witnesses who come, so this Chamber has other information as well. And I can imagine that if you went through this, that you could talk for hours, if not for days or weeks, on the events that have taken place at that time. The Chamber is aware of that. So, as I said, I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, would you please, then, escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any urgent procedural matters to be dealt with at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just the admission of the exhibits, whenever Your Honour wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's a relatively easy one for this witness. So we could do that. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do you want to do that now, Your Honour, or on Monday morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the issue -- we could do it now, but of course there was one complication, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour, yes. There was the question of the objection that I'd made to relevant sections of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that, Mr. Gaynor, of course in the statement -- well, the matter has been dealt with in court and you referred to what is in the additional part. So would it be taken out or would you leave it in? I don't think that it makes that much of a difference, finally, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, I agree, Your Honour. Ms. Loukas referred to the varied paragraphs in her examination, so it might make sense to leave them in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So just as a matter of reference, then, because you asked questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, but they were the matters that of course the Prosecution had referred to, the actual evidence. So -- well, I don't suppose it matters at this point. I think it's probably six of one, half-dozen of the other at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you guide us through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P285A, the witness statement dated 31 January 1999, and P285A.1, the B/C/S translation; P285B, the witness statement dated 19 February 1993, and P285B.1, the English translation; P285C, the handwritten witness statement, and P285C.1, the English translation; P286, the map of Kalinovik; P287, receipt dated 08/05/1992, confirming confiscation of weapon; P287.1, English translation; P288, conclusion of 17 May 1992 session of the war staff of the Kalinovik SO; P288.1, English translation; P289, order from the commander of the Tactical Group, dated 11 June 1992; P289.1, English translation; P290, notification from Serb Republic of BiH, dated 25/06/1992; and P290.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I hear no objections, these exhibits are admitted into evidence. I'd like to ask the parties whether they're available for communication, especially in view of the week not sitting, because the Chamber will further pay attention to them. I'm not saying that insurmountable suddenly has changed, but we'll certainly check whether it's as insurmountable as it looked.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will just indicate that this afternoon Mr. Stewart, Ms. Cmeric and myself have a conference at the United Nations Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you're not allowed to take your mobile.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Where we're not allowed to take our mobile phones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any indication -- but you put them on again once you leave?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed we do, Your Honour. Our conference will be from 3.00 until a quarter to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's good to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So we'll be allowed access to our mobile phones again after that. I will just indicate one thing very quickly, Your Honour. There was one other aspect of a matter that wasn't covered in the statement that I did not go on to, in view of the fact that there was a concession from the Prosecution, and I will just perhaps confirm that with the Prosecution. We can present that on Monday morning. But in view of the time constraints and Your Honour's indicating the situation, I decided not to proceed on another aspect that was not covered in the statement. But it's fairly self-evident that it didn't require any further elaboration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general, the Chamber will accept submissions by the parties to indicate that certain elements were not in earlier statements, et cetera. Of course, if you want to pursue the matter in view of the credibility or the reliability of the witness, then of course it's a different matter. But if it's mainly to establish that it isn't there and then the whole questioning that whether the witness intended to tell everything he knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which of course is impossible anyhow, but -- everything, you know. But that's not necessary for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
